light_description: Japanese-made overdrive/preamp inspired by vintage American tweed amplifiers; official product documentation describes three amp-type modes plus Saturate for broader drive behavior.
Japanese-made hard-drive distortion with three gain-range modes and extensive EQ/pressure controls; official Umbrella Company documentation treats it as a core distortion pedal.
Japanese-made fuzz/distortion with DOPING mid emphasis and 1979 gain-structure switching; official product page provides extensive exterior photography and product history/context.
Original Chocolate Electronics overdrive with punchy mids, strong low end and wide Treble/Bass controls; official documentation traces it to the builder's earlier award-winning DIY work.
All-discrete FET/bipolar light-gain overdrive with broad Treble/Bass shaping and strong response to picking and guitar-volume changes.
Current white-panel overdrive with switchable character and mid/bottom tonal emphasis; official shop provides detailed controls and product photography.
Discrete MOSFET/bipolar overdrive designed for a warm, glossy amplifier-like response with three-position bottom-tone switching.
Hybrid overdrive/fuzz with normal and +1 octave modes, developed from a Big Muff/Rams Head-inspired prototype but differentiated into an original product with strong mid presence.
High-gain fuzz with Fuzz and Insane controls that alter saturation, harmonic behavior, gating and noise characteristics; official shop identifies it as a completely new circuit design.
TS-family-inspired overdrive with Vintage/Fat/Bright modes; official builder interview documents the design intent, naming origin and true-bypass implementation.
Gain/bright-focused drive that the builder describes as closer to a booster but capable of substantial saturation; official interview documents AMP/Saturation behavior and guitar-tone interaction.

Three-transistor fuzz with switchable Fuzz Face-like two-transistor mode and Tone Bender-like three-transistor mode, plus HP and gate controls; official interview provides historical design documentation.
Late-Rams-Head-style fuzz developed from a specific reference specimen; official interview documents the reference concept, tonal behavior and transistor selection approach.
Compact Flying Teapot fuzz model with surviving Japanese dealer specimens and exterior photography; retained as a distinct retail product record.
Handmade Tokyo fuzz with independent front-end boost, shelving tone filter, bias control and concrete enclosure; builder history traces the design back to an earlier Void Fuzz prototype.
Seven-transistor overdrive/fuzz model documented by the builder with multiple individually finished rusted exterior variants; homepage provides repeated exterior photography.
Experimental chaotic dirt device documented by West Tokyo Waves with exterior photographs and a distinct identity within the builder's 2026 catalog.
RoShi Pedals' first pedal, built around Japanese triangle-fuzz history; official documentation provides extensive exterior photography and historical product notes.
Triangle V1-inspired fuzz reproduction developed from a surviving reference specimen; official product page provides multiple exterior photographs and identifies the historical reference lineage.
Compact evolution of RoShi's early Triangle-family work with three-way EQ/voicing switching; official page provides a full exterior image set.
DIZZY TONE-inspired fuzz/distortion based on RoShi Pedals' own vintage specimen, with four interactive controls and documented historical component-selection goals.

AMP-series drive/boost developed to let fuzzes retain articulation while supplying substantial standalone distortion and output; official product page includes exterior photography and detailed use notes.
AMP-series overdrive referencing the Blackface AB763 response, with 6L6/6V6 and Mellow/Drive modes; official product page contains extensive exterior photographs and full controls/specifications.
Natural-drive overdrive using two-stage frequency treatment to shape low-end drive and harmonic edge; official product page includes extensive exterior imagery and detailed control documentation.
